text:
sara: Heads up — I'm prototyping an atomic image-swap flow to avoid orphaned image blobs on customer appliances after a package swap. Want quick feedback on detection + rollback semantics.

miguel: curious what you mean by 'orphaned' here. leftover files on disk? partial writes?

sara: both. common failure mode: swap writes new image files then panics before activation marker written. node restarts with half-new, half-old files. GC later deletes files that look unused and we lose an active version.

nina: we should treat the swap as a 2-phase commit: stage -> verify -> activate. leave previous image intact until activation confirmed.

alex_k: agree. propose write-ahead marker + atomic rename for final activation. e.g. create /var/lib/redwood/_staged/<id> then when verified rename to /var/lib/redwood/images/<id>. rename is atomic on same FS so avoids partial visibility.

pat: edge-case: what if rename succeeds but process crashes before updating k8s CR / operator state? operator will see mismatch and might GC old image. need idempotent reconcile logic.

sara: right. operator should rely on filesystem markers and node heartbeats: only GC when a quorum of nodes report new <id> active AND operator sees activation marker in cluster state.

miguel: detection for orphaning: periodic scan that looks for image dirs with no active-ref in operator state for > grace_period. but we should avoid sweeping recent swaps. maybe include a "staged_at" timestamp and an origin node id.

nina: also add a small verification step that checks content checksums after rename. we already store per-image manifest with sha256; verify against that before promoting as active.

alex_k: sample marker flow:
```
# on agent
write /var/lib/redwood/_staged/<id>/manifest.json
download blobs to /var/lib/redwood/_staged/<id>/blobs/
verify checksums
fsync directory
rename /var/lib/redwood/_staged/<id> -> /var/lib/redwood/images/<id>
write /run/redwood/active-ids/<id>.marker (local marker)
notify operator: ImageSwapRequest -> applying
```

pat: operator CRD should have states: pending -> applying -> activated -> failed. include fields: attempted_nodes (list), success_count, last_error, staged_timestamp. GC only allowed when state == activated and retention_window expired.

miguel: what about encryption keys / attestation? if we delete old blobs we should ensure new version's attestation proves correct decryption. suggestion: require device-local attestation token signed by KMS before GC of previous secrets.

sara: yes. GC flow should include attestation certificate and timestamp. add a safety net: when node reports activation, it must send an attestation blob signed by device key. operator verifies before marking node as successful.

deploy-bot: :information_source: rollout noted for onprem-image-swap-prototype, env=staging, batch=10 nodes.

alex_k: one more failure mode: power loss during large blob stream can leave sparse partial files. solution: download into temp filenames (.partial) and use atomic rename per blob, or store blob into content-addressed store keyed by hash so partial writes don't masquerade as valid content.

nina: CA-store + single writer lock for an image id works well. and retention policy: keep last N activated image ids per customer to allow fast rollback. N configurable (default 2).

pat: rollout plan: stage to staging with batch activation -> wait 10m -> quorum verify -> schedule GC after 24h. operator must expose manual override to force rollback if activation_count < threshold.

sara: plan sounds good. action items: (1) alex_k to draft agent marker + rename snippets for the agent pkg, (2) pat to update CRD fields & GC policy, (3) miguel/nina to write attestation verification contract. I'll prototype a PoC on staging this week. :rocket:

miguel: :+1:

nina: will help test failure injection for partial-renames/powercuts.

pat: I'll update the operator reconciler to tolerate transient mismatches and avoid premature GC.

sara: thanks all — will post a short RFC doc when PoC stabilizes.
